answer: Sybil resistance in agent economies often rests on a per-identity capital bond, posted before any agent can earn and slashed on the first proven double-answer. A newcomer cannot harvest an orchard of synthetic identities, since each one needs the same collateral plus its own work receipt. Attacker cost scales linearly with clones while honest yield does not, so profit turns negative once fakes pass real demand. Linked accounts also expose one operator, forfeiting a whole ridge of keys at once. Every identity leaves a crystal of attestations graders can replay, so copied claims stand out.
